rules.when: A trivial mechanical edit with no judgement: a rename, a typo, a formatting or lint-only fix, a version bump, a one-line CI or config value change, or copying text the ticket spells out exactly.
rules.why: Workers that only execute run on Sonnet 5.5. Low effort is enough for an edit with no judgement. A one-line CI change cost $3.11 on Opus.

rules.when: Simple, fully specified work: a small UI or copy change, a test for behaviour that already exists, documentation, a small bug whose cause is already known, or a change the ticket describes step by step.
rules.why: Clear scope and low ambiguity; Sonnet does this well at a fraction of Opus.

rules.when: Needs real judgement: a product or design decision, architecture or a refactor across modules, auth, permissions or security, a database schema or data migration, money, clinical or legal logic, a bug whose cause is still unknown, or a retry after a failed review round.
rules.why: Firstmate gives Opus 5.5 only to a worker whose task needs judgement, because a wrong call there is expensive. Normal context window, never 1M.
